### Upper bound: $n\le 302$

Double-count the quantity $\sum_{v} d_B(v)$ over all 500 cells. Each black cell $u$ is counted once by each of its $\deg_G(u)$ grid-neighbors, so

$$\sum_{v\text{ all}} d_B(v)=\sum_{u\text{ black}} \deg_G(u).$$

Since every cell has at most 2 black neighbors, $\sum_v d_B(v)\le 2\cdot 500=1000$, hence

$$\sum_{u\text{ black}} \deg_G(u)\le 1000. \tag{1}$$

In the $5\times 100$ grid: 4 corner cells have degree 2; $202$ boundary (non-corner) cells have degree 3; $294$ interior cells have degree 4. Let $c,e,i$ be the numbers of black cells of these three types, so $n=c+e+i$, with $c\le 4$, $e\le 202$. Then

$$\sum_{u\text{ black}} \deg_G(u)=2c+3e+4i=4n-2c-e.$$

Combining with (1): $4n-2c-e\le 1000$, so $4n\le 1000+2c+e\le 1000+8+202=1210$, giving

$$n\le \left\lfloor \frac{1210}{4}\right\rfloor = 302.$$

- **the entire perimeter** (all of row 1, row 5, column 1, column 100) — 206 cells;

*Row 2, white cells* $(2,j),\,2\le j\le 99$: $(1,j)$ black; $(3,j)$ black for $3\le j\le 98$, white for $j\in\{2,99\}$; horizontal neighbors $(2,j-1),(2,j+1)$ white except $(2,1),(2,100)$ black at $j=2,99$.  
- $j=2$: $(1,2)$B, $(3,2)$W, $(2,1)$B → 2.

$$\sum_{v\text{ all}} d_B(v)=\sum_{u\text{ black}} \deg_G(u).$$
